text: An engineering overview of the platform, its applications, and the workflows that turn operational activity into reusable assets.
OperatorOS centralizes authority while purpose-built applications retain their own work models. The intended value is less re-entry, clearer ownership, and evidence that survives the handoff.
Identity, tenants, roles, subscriptions, entitlements, launch policy, and audit have one parent authority.
Service revenue, IT resolution, and healthcare operations remain separate main-module workflows.
Reviewed proof, scripts, knowledge, training cases, and campaign packages become durable work products.
Architecture and platform: pages 3–7. Module inventories and case studies: pages 8–33. Resolution Intelligence: page 34. Evaluation and evidence: pages 35–38.

Case-study method: all 42 scenarios are illustrative, not customer testimonials. Expected outputs are workflow goals; measurement suggestions are not reported results. Feature descriptions are grounded in repository contracts and implementation records.
The map shows product scope and access class. Actual access is a server decision; an application category is not a promise that every tenant receives it.

Current commerce separates the selected core product, companion grants, and seats. Legacy plan compatibility is a separate path. No pricing quote or all-modules entitlement is implied by this overview.
Next.js web surfaces and a private Fastify API operate as one platform deployment. Module hosts present distinct products; they do not become independent identity or billing systems.
Same-origin /api requestsHost-only application session
Next.js on public port 5000Exact registered host routing
Fastify on private port 5001Auth + tenant + role + entitlement
Tenant-scoped records, constraints, audit, durable jobs, outbox/inbox, and ordered database releases.
Payments, telephony, AI, email, scanning, and storage retain independent setup and acceptance gates.
SSO: a 60-second opaque code is single-use and bound to exact callback, state, nonce, PKCE S256, environment, tenant, module, and entitlement. Redemption revalidates authority.

Isolation: host-only Secure/HttpOnly cookies; no ambient parent-domain cookie. Server-resolved tenant predicates govern reads, writes, constraints, transactions, and audit. A requested tenant ID is never authority.
A common control plane reduces duplicated security and business logic while keeping module records, roles, and outcomes explicit.
Central sign-in, session lifecycle, role checks, account status, MFA/revocation controls, and exact-host SSO.
Validated memberships, organization selection, module grants, subscription/seat policy, and server-owned launch decisions.
Organization/contact identity reused by supported applications; shared contact edits avoid automatic rewriting of historical reports.
Private attachments, configured scanning, durable work queues, usage accounting, export artifacts, and explicit failure/retry states.
Platform Stripe authority stays separate from module business payments; stored configuration never proves external delivery.
Platform audit, shared activity/notifications, tenant messenger, administrative visibility, and scoped record-to-record handoffs.
Operational intelligence today: deterministic workday briefs rank recorded exceptions and point to the next action. They do not silently invoice, charge, send, assign, or execute.
Ten registered workflow contracts connect selected records. Each result remains a specific draft, ticket, attachment, or package with a reviewed source version.

Delivery contract: recheck both applications and source access at queue and delivery; reject changed sources; deduplicate the business operation; retain signed event context and scoped results. Training handoffs require manager review. Live-call handoffs reject simulations.
These are evaluation scenarios using synthetic or approved data. They do not report customer deployments or measured results.
One engineer, several workspaces
An engineer belongs to two organizations and must reach the right module without mixing records or permissions.
Authenticate centrally, select the organization, and launch an entitled module. Follow a deep link and then return to My Apps; switching organization requires a fresh module authorization.
A host-specific session bound to the intended tenant and module, with server-side checks on every protected action.
Cross-tenant denial; deep-link continuity; absence of repeat credential entry.
A customer shared across workflows
A service customer appears in commercial records, a campaign brand, and field proof, each with different work history.

Use the supported shared customer selector in TradeFlowKit, BrandForge OS, and SnapProofOS. Update the shared contact intentionally and verify current projections without rewriting approved historical reports.
One reusable customer identity with independent module records and preserved historical evidence.
Duplicate identity creation; contact consistency; historical report stability.
A retry without a duplicate result
A reviewed cross-module transfer is interrupted after submission and another authorized person attempts the same outcome.
Queue the supported handoff with its source version. Inspect status and the destination link, then exercise the allowed retry path; changed sources and revoked access should fail closed.
A traceable, deduplicated destination result for supported tenant-owned workflows; actor-scoped campaign generation remains distinct.
Duplicate records; stale-source rejection; recoverable retry behavior.
A shared operations workspace for service businesses: customer context, execution, commercial documents, and collections remain connected throughout the job lifecycle.
Capture leads; qualify and convert opportunities; use shared customer identity, contacts, search, and bounded CSV imports.
Schedule and assign jobs; retain owners, dates, status, recurring templates, pause controls, and run history.
Track job-scoped tasks, dependencies, comments, tags, workflow transitions, and personal or shared saved views.
Build multi-line quotes; record decisions; convert to jobs or invoices with duplicate-safe server operations.
Maintain invoice items, partial/full payment records, balances, numbering, and history; connected settlement needs provider acceptance.
Use scoped public views, customer portals, and consent-aware email/SMS outbox actions with explicit delivery state.
Inspect workload and revenue from persisted records; export invoice CSV, QuickBooks IIF, and Xero-oriented CSV files.
Create SnapProofOS work from a job, return the approved PDF, and use guarded archive/restore workflows.
One traceable chain from customer request through work, proof, invoice, and recorded settlement.
Live payments and outbound delivery require configured, accepted providers. Accounting exports are files, not live QuickBooks/Xero synchronization. Recording a sent state is not email delivery.
Problem → workflow → expected output. Measurements are suggested pilot checks, not claimed results.
The unbilled service call
A field-service team finishes a repair, but the invoice handoff is lost between the technician and office.
Link the customer, job, task completion, and quote. Use the workday brief to find completed jobs without an invoice, then review and create the commercial record.
A job-linked invoice with an owner and an explicit balance; no automatic charge is implied.
Completed jobs without invoices; days from completion to invoice.
Recurring maintenance without duplicate jobs
A contractor repeats the same service at several customer sites and recreates the work manually each month.
Define recurring job templates, inspect the next run, and let the supported scheduler create the dated job. Pause a schedule during an outage and inspect its history before resuming.
Repeatable work records whose schedule/run identity prevents replay from creating duplicates.
Manual setup time; duplicate jobs per scheduled run.
A defensible proof-to-payment handoff
An office needs to show what was done before following up on an unpaid installation.
Create SnapProofOS work from the originating job. Review the captured evidence and approved report, return its PDF to that exact job, then review invoice and recorded payment state.
Commercial context and approved proof remain linked. A report attachment does not assert customer receipt.
Jobs with linked approved proof; time spent reconstructing an invoice history.

An MSP and IT operations console that binds support work to client, configuration, network, procedure, and evidence context. Resolution Intelligence preserves what actually happened, including failed attempts.
Manage client/site-linked tickets, assignments, comments, time, requester updates, and accountable closeout.
Track typed configurations, asset context, warranty/renewal dates, lifecycle changes, and related records.
Maintain network, subnet, address, and topology relationships as documented operational context.
Edit knowledge articles and runbooks with revisions, backlinks, review, approval, publication, and private attachments.
Import structured closeouts with screened source material, immutable revisions, validation, warnings, failures, and side effects.
Search identifiers and narrative; inspect evidence, components, action chronology, revision history, and native links.
Preview deterministic KB/runbook drafts, retain source citations, link multiple incidents, and block stale-source approval.
Use persisted dashboards, client reports, portal/status workflows, scoped API tokens, and signed outbound webhooks.
A resolution record that explains the fix, failed paths, uncertainty, verification, and reusable guidance.

Runbooks do not execute scripts. Inventory is not live discovery or endpoint control. Phase 5 semantic retrieval is source-implemented and provider-disabled; ordinary exact/text search is independent.
Problem → workflow → expected output. Measurements are suggested pilot checks, not claimed results.
A recurring application failure
A second engineer inherits a symptom that resembles an earlier incident, but a copied final fix omits a harmful intermediate step.
Search the exact error or component. Review the prior chronology, failed action, observed side effect, warning, and validation before choosing a procedure for the new client issue.
An evidence-informed plan with uncertainty retained. The previous outcome does not prove the same root cause now.
Time to relevant evidence; repeated failed actions avoided during a reviewed pilot.
A client infrastructure handover
An MSP technician leaves and the replacement must reconstruct dependencies from tickets and isolated notes.
Connect the client's sites, configurations, IPAM records, lifecycle dates, and versioned documentation. Link current tickets and supporting evidence, then prepare a client-facing operational report.
A navigable service context with named records and a reusable procedure trail.
Time to locate the affected system, owner, and current approved procedure.
From one repair to a maintained runbook
A difficult incident is resolved, but the team needs repeatable guidance that will not silently drift from its source.
Preview an evidence-derived runbook, review the cited sections, save a draft, and submit it through approval. When source evidence changes, inspect the stale warning and prepare current guidance.
A reviewed document with source-revision links and access inherited from every linked incident.
Time from closeout to reviewed guidance; stale-source publications prevented.

Healthcare operations coordination for facilities, equipment, supplies, departments, and vendors. The work model captures operational ownership and response history while minimizing patient information.
Maintain directory-linked organizations, facilities, requesters, departments, and operational context.
Create numbered requests with structured classification, equipment-issue prefill, tags, and supporting records.
Route work to an accountable team or owner; prioritize through queues, filters, saved views, and bulk actions.
Track service targets, time, at-risk work, escalation paths, and response history.
Keep internal coordination separate from requester-facing replies; retain private attachments and work history.
Associate operational assets with facility issues, supply requests, service vendors, and department needs.
Use operational knowledge, persisted dashboards, configuration, preferences, trend reporting, and exports.
Accept operations-only CallCommand requests and prepare privacy-reviewed resolved-work drafts for FaultlineLab.
A resolved operational request with accountable ownership, response timing, and an inspectable work history.
No patient chart, clinical decision, EHR/PACS integration, or HIPAA certification is claimed. Direct Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, IMAP, and SendGrid mailbox intake is unavailable in this release.
Problem → workflow → expected output. Measurements are suggested pilot checks, not claimed results.
An equipment issue between departments
An imaging department reports an unavailable workstation or equipment accessory; responsibility spans facilities and a vendor.
Create an operations-only request, associate the facility and asset, assign an owner, set the service target, and retain vendor coordination and requester updates in the work record.
A visible accountable path to restoring operational availability without storing a patient chart.
Unassigned age; response time; handoffs without a named owner.
A supply delay before a busy shift
A department has an unresolved supply request with a deadline, while the next shift sees only a message thread.
Classify the supply need, associate the department and vendor, record the due target, and use the queue to escalate the delay. Close the request with the actual resolution and timing.
A shared request history that survives shift changes and shows what remains open.
Overdue operational requests; time spent reconstructing shift context.
Learning from repeated facility incidents
Several resolved facilities requests reveal a recurring troubleshooting mistake useful for staff training.
Review the operational history and select a suitable resolved request. Managers with access to both applications review privacy and prepare an unpublished FaultlineLab draft for trainer revision.
A controlled training starting point; the imported first revision cannot publish directly.
Repeat incident patterns identified; reviewed training cases produced.

A garage and automotive diagnostics workspace for vehicle history, structured tests, workshop records, and shareable proof. Torque Assist adds governed guidance when its provider and credit controls are configured.
Record vehicles, mileage, owner concerns, repairs, maintenance, and service chronology.
Organize symptoms, codes, observations, likely causes, tests, findings, and verification.
Request context-aware diagnostic guidance through OperatorOS-owned AI and usage/token accounting.
Track build stages, parts, labor, costs, notes, and supporting media.
Create workshop exports and repair records; use supported live-bay and sharing workflows.
Maintain profiles, preferences, posts, comments, reactions, follows/blocks, private media, and moderation records.
Search and save listings; contact sellers; retain conversations, expiry, reports, and listing history.
Prepare diagnostic proof in SnapProofOS and reviewed automotive challenge drafts in FaultlineLab.
A repair narrative that separates symptoms, measured observations, work performed, and verified outcome.

Physical tests and repair judgment remain with the technician. Marketplace listings do not imply escrow, shipping, buyer protection, or reputation guarantees. AI and native-device acceptance are separate gates.
Problem → workflow → expected output. Measurements are suggested pilot checks, not claimed results.
Diagnose before replacing parts
A shop receives an intermittent vehicle complaint with several plausible causes and incomplete prior history.
Record symptoms, codes, and earlier work, choose the next physical test, and capture its findings. Use Assist only as reviewed guidance when configured; record the actual repair and verification.
A test-driven diagnostic record that explains why a repair was selected.
Diagnostic steps with recorded findings; repeat visits for the same complaint.
A build that outlives its original owner
A custom vehicle changes hands after months of modifications spread across receipts and photos.
Organize stages, parts, labor, costs, media, and service entries in the build journal. Produce a workshop export or controlled repair record for the receiving party.
A coherent modification and service history with traceable supporting material.
Missing part/service records; time required to reconstruct a modification.
A verified diagnosis becomes training
A mechanic resolves a difficult fault that would make a useful diagnostic exercise for apprentices.
Finish the diagnostic record with recorded tests and findings. A manager reviews privacy and transfers a training draft to FaultlineLab, then edits the narrative and evidence before publication.
An unpublished automotive case that retains diagnostic structure without bypassing trainer review.
Reviewed cases created from real work; learner investigation quality.

A diagnostic challenge environment for technical practice. Versioned scenarios, persistent investigation traces, and server scoring let a reviewer inspect the reasoning path as well as the final answer.
Discover published challenges through search, filters, sorting, authored packs, and daily selection.
Resume standard, daily, preview, assignment, and Chaos-mode attempts across refresh and restart.
Select diagnostic actions, reveal clues, record findings, use progressive hints, and submit a conclusion.
Evaluate submitted work against the versioned scenario and retain append-only attempt evidence.
Assign cases, inspect learning progress and badges, and select further practice from observed results.
Validate, preview, publish, retire, import, and export controlled challenge versions.
Review attempts and outcome history; export material for coaching and team discussion.
Convert reviewed TechDeck, PulseDesk, and TorqueShed records into private first-draft challenges.
A replayable investigation record showing which evidence the learner inspected and how the answer was reached.

Training scores are scenario performance, not accredited certification or production authorization. Imported incidents require privacy review and a revised trainer-approved version before publication.
Problem → workflow → expected output. Measurements are suggested pilot checks, not claimed results.
A repeatable technician onboarding exercise
Two new engineers know the terminology, but the lead needs to see how they investigate an ambiguous failure.
Assign the same versioned challenge, compare action sequences and missed evidence, and discuss the submitted cause and response using the retained attempt trace.
A concrete coaching conversation grounded in observed diagnostic choices.
Missed critical clues; unnecessary actions; score progression on comparable cases.
Turn a resolved incident into an exercise
An internal outage contains a useful lesson but also client names and sensitive operational details.
Use the supported resolved-work handoff, review privacy, and revise the private draft. Validate and preview the case before publishing a controlled version for the intended learners.
Reusable practice material with a deliberate editorial and privacy boundary.
Time from incident review to approved exercise; privacy findings caught before publication.
Diagnose under changing conditions
Experienced staff need practice handling incomplete clues and disruption without changing a production environment.
Use a suitable Chaos or daily challenge. Retain the investigation trace, inspect the result, and repeat a targeted exercise where the original reasoning missed a signal.
A safe training record that exposes decision habits under scenario pressure.
Recovery of investigation after new evidence; repeat occurrence of the same reasoning error.

A browser-based 8-ball companion with real gameplay, persistent match state, and protected online rooms. Its engineering interest lies in deterministic simulation, server validation, and recovery across interruptions.
Practice shot selection, aim, power, and cue-ball control in the Canvas play surface.
Play against seeded CPU behavior with the supported rules and deterministic physics.
Share a device for turn-based play with visible match and turn state.
Create or join protected rooms through OperatorOS identity and access controls.
Use durable snapshots/events and independent server re-simulation of submitted actions.
Recover supported room state after interruptions and enforce room lifecycle limits.
Use touch-friendly controls, spin/English, audio options, and performance settings.
Keep supported profile/result records and use the installable web-app experience.
A recoverable match with consistent turn and shot state across the supported play surfaces.
A community benefit with no wagering, paid competition, prizes, or independently certified rankings. Online two-device and performance acceptance should be demonstrated in the target environment.
Problem → workflow → expected output. Measurements are suggested pilot checks, not claimed results.
A five-minute practice break
An engineer wants a short break between long support sessions without setting up another account.
Launch the free companion through OperatorOS and enter Free Shoot. Practice a repeatable shot while adjusting aim, power, and English with the supported controls.
Immediate, self-contained practice inside the same account ecosystem.
Time from launcher to first playable shot; input responsiveness on the chosen device.
A teammate disconnects mid-match
Two coworkers play in a protected online room and one browser loses connectivity.
Play through normal server-checked actions, reconnect within the supported room lifetime, and inspect the restored turn and match state from durable snapshots and events.
A recoverable game state rather than an unverified client-only continuation.
State agreement after reconnect; abandoned matches caused by recoverable disconnects.
A practical state-consistency demo
A team wants a small, understandable example of authoritative state and replay validation.
Use an authorized test session to examine normal shot submission, server re-simulation, and refresh recovery. Compare visible state across clients without claiming a formal security assessment.
An accessible demonstration of client input, authoritative checks, and durable state.
Consistent ball/turn state across refreshes and the two test clients.
A brand and campaign workspace for reusable context, reviewed assets, and coordinated delivery packages. The catalog uses the compact name BrandForgeOS; both refer to the same application.
Maintain brand kits, positioning, voice, offers, and audience personas; associate approved shared customer identity.
Create campaign briefs, objectives, channels, budgets, timelines, and related landing content.
Develop copy variants, calls to action, ad prompts, strategy, and creative directions through guided modes.
Preview wordmark, lockup, badge, and monogram compositions; export editable SVG and standard/2x PNG.
Manage draft/review/approval states, comments, assets, activity, and recoverable selected logos.
Organize delivery work and reuse global/custom templates subject to the applicable entitlements.
Track entered results, recommendations, and campaign reports; create controlled exports.
Transfer a campaign into Deploy Ops with copy, visual-production briefs, work items, and an approval starting state.
A reusable brand context and reviewed campaign package with clear ownership and delivery decisions.

Direct advertising, social, email, analytics, and CRM delivery are unavailable in this release. Canva/Figma use manual file import. Generated assets require review; a scheduled item is not publication.
Problem → workflow → expected output. Measurements are suggested pilot checks, not claimed results.
One offer, several inconsistent messages
An MSP launches a service package, but website copy, sales emails, and social drafts describe different benefits.
Define the audience, offer, proof points, and voice once. Build campaign variants from that context, review the claims together, and export the approved materials for each external channel.
A coherent campaign kit whose variants can be traced back to agreed positioning.
Review rounds caused by inconsistent claims; time to produce an approved variant.
Agency work without cross-client confusion
A small team manages several customers and repeatedly copies brand details between disconnected documents.
Associate each brand with the correct shared customer, maintain distinct personas and offers, and retain campaign assets, comments, and review states under the authorized organization.
Customer-linked creative context and an inspectable approval history.
Misattributed assets; time required to locate the latest approved brand direction.
From campaign approval to a launch package
A campaign is approved, but the coordinator still needs channel copy, production briefs, and assigned launch work.
Review the current campaign and queue the Deploy Ops handoff. Inspect the returned package, complete missing production items, and export only after the team checks the resulting materials.
A coordinated execution package; no advertising spend or external publication occurs automatically.
Time from approval to handoff; missing deliverables discovered before launch.

A field-work and evidence workflow for customer jobs, dated captures, findings, review, and branded reports. Controlled sharing is tied to approved report snapshots rather than unrestricted raw evidence.
Select shared customer identity, create proof work, assign field tasks, and retain job context.
Collect photos, private notes, files, observations, parts, labor, and dated work context.
Apply type/signature checks, private storage, scan state, and SHA-256 verification through shared services.
Submit evidence, inspect findings, record comments, and move reports through authorized review and approval.
Generate approved PDF and DOCX documents from the selected report snapshot and template.
Create expiring and revocable report links; inspect access history without exposing the private source library.
Retain hash-linked custody history, immutable report context, archive controls, retention, and legal-hold state.
Receive TradeFlowKit job or TorqueShed diagnostic context; return the exact approved PDF to its originating job.
A branded, approved proof package whose included evidence can be traced to the field assignment.
Storage, scanning, and document workers need acceptance. A share link is not proof of delivery or receipt. Hash-linked history supports integrity review; it is not a legal-admissibility guarantee.
Problem → workflow → expected output. Measurements are suggested pilot checks, not claimed results.
A field installation with incomplete closeout
An engineer completes a network cabinet installation, but photos and labor notes remain scattered across devices.
Create the customer job, assign capture work, add dated photos and notes, record findings and costs, and assemble the customer-facing template for review.
One approved report with supporting job context instead of a loose image folder.
Jobs missing required evidence; time from site departure to approved report.
Review a disputed service outcome
A customer questions what was included in a repair or inspection performed several weeks earlier.
Open the authorized job and inspect its captured evidence, comments, custody history, and approved report snapshot. Generate or retrieve the exact document relevant to the reviewed work.
An inspectable record of what was captured and approved, without assuming the record proves causation.
Time to reconstruct the work package; gaps in the evidence-to-report chain.
Share the report, control the access
A project manager needs to give a customer a finished report while keeping internal notes and raw captures private.
Approve the snapshot, generate the requested format, and deliberately create an expiring report share. Deliver it through the team's approved channel and revoke access when appropriate.
A bounded customer report link with expiry, revocation, and access history.
Unrestricted evidence links created; share expiry/revocation behavior in the pilot.
A source-based study workspace that turns supplied notes into complete study packs and persistent practice. Built-in creation remains useful without the optional shared AI service.
Organize source material, course/exam context, titles, descriptions, and reusable study sets.
Create summaries, key terms, flashcards, multiple-choice questions, short answers, review sheets, and plans.
Use deterministic creation or configured shared AI refinement with validation, provenance, and fallback behavior.
Practice with keyboard/touch controls and retain known/learning state and session progress.
Use server-scored attempts, inspect explanations and missed answers, and retain retry/history records.
Track date-based study plans, exam countdowns, streaks, usage, and learning trends.
Edit, search, filter, duplicate, regenerate, archive, restore, and remove supported study material.
Export study sets and supported progress/results as JSON or entitlement-gated CSV.
A reusable study pack plus a history of practice and quiz results that identifies material needing another pass.
Generated material needs source review. AI requires shared-service setup. No outside citations, accredited qualification, automatic mastery judgment, or invented classroom/group workflow is claimed.
Problem → workflow → expected output. Measurements are suggested pilot checks, not claimed results.
Prepare for a platform handover
An engineer must learn an internal service before joining the support rotation.
Supply approved, non-secret operating notes, build a study pack, correct the generated material against the source, and use flashcards and a quiz to reveal weak areas.
A repeatable learning aid with an inspectable source basis and saved practice history.
Questions missed by topic; preparation time using the same approved material.
Turn a long workshop into practice
A technical workshop produces useful notes, but participants rarely revisit the full document.
Create a focused set from the approved workshop material. Review terms, short answers, and the review sheet; schedule study around the intended date and inspect the quiz explanations.
Multiple ways to rehearse the same material without claiming the generated pack is authoritative.
Study sessions completed; repeated mistakes after source corrections.
Keep learning when AI is unavailable
A team wants a study workflow before external AI service approval is complete.
Use built-in pack creation, manually refine the material, and practice through the existing flashcard and quiz paths. Export the set for review and retain usage/history in the workspace.
A functioning study process that does not depend on live model access.
Completion of the study workflow with AI disabled; content corrections found in review.
A campaign-package and readiness workspace. Despite the name, its current product scope is coordinated campaign preparation and human-verified delivery records, not software deployment automation.
Start from reusable templates; define audience, offer, action, tone, channels, and launch date.
Prepare landing, ad, email, SMS, social, FAQ, flyer, and call-to-action copy.
Create up to nine visual briefs, with included plan items made explicit.
Retain saved packages, revisions, source context, approved inputs, and related private assets.
Assign phases, milestones, owners, required files, tasks, and dependencies.
Calculate readiness from recorded conditions and approvals; inspect missing prerequisites before a launch transition.
Download supported text, Markdown, JSON, and CSV packages with checksum and audit context.
Receive BrandForgeOS campaign handoffs and record externally confirmed completion with a reference.
A reviewed campaign kit, explicit launch checklist, and verifiable export for the people using publishing tools.
Does not deploy software, change DNS, publish sites/ads, send campaigns, or buy media. A readiness score reflects recorded package conditions; external completion needs a person's verified reference.
Problem → workflow → expected output. Measurements are suggested pilot checks, not claimed results.
Launch an MSP service offer
A new managed service needs consistent landing copy, FAQs, ads, and a practical launch checklist.
Define the business brief and channels, generate the package, review every claim, assign production tasks, and export the approved material to the people operating the external tools.
A coordinated campaign package with clear owners and outstanding work.
Missing launch assets; time from accepted brief to reviewed export.
Find the launch blocker before launch day
Copy is finished, but required artwork and approval are missing from a campaign nearing its deadline.
Use the execution workspace to inspect required files, dependencies, owners, and computed readiness. Complete and review the missing work before recording the launch transition.
An evidence-based readiness decision with the unresolved dependency visible.
Late blockers found before the deadline; launch transitions with incomplete prerequisites.
Hand a campaign to another team
A campaign coordinator needs a clean package for an agency or internal publishing team.
Review the current package, create a verified export, and use the team's normal delivery channel. After publication, a person checks the external result and records its reference.
A traceable artifact handoff and separately recorded external confirmation.
Rework caused by missing copy or context; exports lacking a reviewed version.

A business receptionist, call-intelligence, and MSP intake workspace with simulations, flow design, follow-up records, and explicit provider readiness. Real calls require accepted telephony, AI, and billing configuration.
Define business knowledge, hours, greetings, behavior, and approved routing destinations.
Prepare conversation paths, test a no-cost simulated call, and correct routing before live enablement.
Manage number setup, readiness checks, capacity, usage, service health, and deliberate go-live controls.
Search history; inspect summaries, timelines, transcripts, consent state, outcomes, and reviewed analysis.
Review leads, tasks, alerts, and staff actions with clear ownership and retained call context.
Convert eligible analyzed provider calls into reviewed TradeFlowKit, TechDeck, or operations-only PulseDesk work.
Use approved lines, SupportLinks, Directory-backed organization/contact association, local cases, and operator screen-pop.
Use signed callbacks, durable retry/outbox records, kill switches, evidence history, and explicit test/live distinctions.
A call outcome with retained context and a clearly owned next action, distinguished from any test simulation.

Live Twilio/OpenAI/Stripe and callback acceptance remain separate. Simulations cannot create production call handoffs. BMS delivery and privileged Datto/Graph/AD actions are not accepted by the MSP foundation.
Problem → workflow → expected output. Measurements are suggested pilot checks, not claimed results.
Test after-hours intake before activation
An MSP wants consistent after-hours intake but needs to inspect what the receptionist will ask and where it will route work.
Configure hours, approved knowledge, and escalation paths. Run simulations, inspect captured answers and routing, and correct the flow before the separate provider go-live checks.
A reviewed receptionist configuration and test outcome without purchasing or placing a live call.
Required intake fields captured in simulations; incorrect routes found before activation.
A real call becomes a support ticket
After provider acceptance, a caller describes an issue that should enter the technical queue with usable context.
Review the completed, analyzed provider call and choose the TechDeck handoff. The system reloads the reviewed version and checks access before creating the destination ticket.
A linked ticket from an eligible real call; simulator records are rejected.
Calls without an owner; manual re-entry time; duplicate destination tickets.
Separate caller context from privileged action
An MSP caller requests urgent account help, but caller recognition must not become authorization for a reset.
Use approved intake channels and organization/contact association to capture the issue and open a local case. Review screen-pop and evidence, then use the independently authorized support process.
Useful intake context without an automatic identity reset or endpoint action.
Unassociated cases; quality of issue capture; privileged actions requiring explicit separate approval.

A script-authoring and governance workspace for reusable IT automation. Static analysis, immutable versions, explicit review, and audited downloads preserve the boundary between preparing source and executing it.
Organize PowerShell, Python, batch, and shell assets with source/provenance context.
Create or import source and record the purpose, prerequisites, expected behavior, risk, and rollback.
Pin the exact revision, content identity, and change context used by subsequent review and download.
Inspect findings and risk indicators before submitting a script version for approval.
Submit, approve, reject, or retire scripts under tenant-admin controls with recorded decisions.
Allow only the approved current version to be downloaded; retain integrity and download audit history.
Request drafts through shared AI, idempotency, and usage controls; generated source remains unapproved.
Create a non-executing draft runbook and protected file-integrity record from an approved script revision.
A specific approved source version with requirements, review findings, rollback context, and an auditable download.

OperatorOS does not execute this source in the browser, API, server, or customer environment. Static analysis is not proof of safety. Execution and endpoint acceptance belong to a separately authorized tool.
Problem → workflow → expected output. Measurements are suggested pilot checks, not claimed results.
Retire the copied desktop script
Several technicians keep slightly different copies of a maintenance script with unclear origin and prerequisites.

Import the reviewed source, document requirements and rollback, run static checks, and submit an exact version for approval. Technicians download the approved current revision for their authorized environment.
One governed automation asset with a visible version and decision history.
Untracked variants; downloads without an approved current version.
Use AI without auto-approving its output
An engineer wants help drafting a repetitive inventory script but must inspect its behavior before distribution.
Request a draft through the configured shared AI service, inspect its source, address static findings, and submit the corrected immutable revision to a tenant administrator.
A reviewable draft that cannot become an approved download merely because a model generated it.
Findings corrected before approval; generated drafts distributed without review.
Preserve procedure beside the code
A useful script exists, but new staff do not know when to use it or how to interpret its output.
Select an approved current revision and create the supported TechDeck draft runbook. Review its prerequisites and handling instructions in TechDeck before publishing the procedure.
Linked source identity and reviewed guidance; the handoff performs no execution.
Approved assets with current runbook context; source/runbook version mismatches.

A reconstructed application for a discreet call to a person's own verified phone. Source/local workflow evidence exists, but the production catalog remains unavailable and these scenarios describe gated behavior.
